history.period: Discovered July 2004; no temple structure - open-air lingam with installed well, havan kund and bells
history.summary: CSV row 73 and CSV row 71 are DUPLICATES of the same shrine — the same 25-ft natural Shiva Linga in Kardo Forest, called both 'Siddheshwar Nath Temple' and 'Shiva Linga Temple' in travel sources. Documented here under the real documented name, Siddeshwar Nath Temple (Kardo Forest, Ziro). The lingam — said to be the world's tallest natural Shiv Lingam, 25 ft tall and 22 ft in circumference at an altitude of 5,754 ft on the Apatani Plateau — was discovered in July 2004 when local Nepali woodcutter Prem Subha's felled tree fell against the stone. Named Siddeshwar Nath / Siddheshwar Mahadev; devotees cite the Rudra Khand of the Shiva Purana (17th chapter of the 9th khand, Lingalaya in 'Arunachal'). No temple building stands around the lingam; a well, havan kund and bells have been installed, with priests present dawn till dusk. Neighbouring natural rock formations resemble Parvati and Ganesha (verify), and water flows from the lingam's base. The Archaeological Department reportedly studied it and found the base ~4 ft deep. Filed separately from row 71 per instructions; the two files describe the same shrine.

name: Siddeshwar Nath Temple (Kardo Forest, Ziro)
town: Kardo, Ziro Valley (CSV town 'Ziro' accepted - shrine is ~2.4 miles / ~14 km from Hapoli/Ziro in Kardo Forest; accounts differ, verify)
town_description: Ziro (Hapoli is the township) is the headquarters of Lower Subansiri district and home to the Apatani tribe's famous paddy-fish cultivation, a UNESCO tentative World Heritage site. The cool, scenic Ziro Valley hosts the Ziro Music Festival and the Siddeshwar Nath shrine in the dense Kardo Forest a few kilometres away.

travel.airport: Lilabari Airport (IXI), Assam - ~120-125 km, 4-5 hours by taxi/shared vehicle (per Incredible India); helicopter service Guwahati-Naharlagun also listed by the district.
travel.railway: Harmuti Junction (HMY), Assam - ~100 km (per Incredible India); Naharlagun is the nearest railhead per district tourism.
travel.road: Drive Itanagar (~100 km) / Naharlagun / Guwahati (445-470 km) to Ziro by bus or shared Sumo; then a trek into Kardo Forest - the path is described as treacherous, requiring stamina (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for the trek; Shravan (July-August) and Maha Shivaratri draw crowds but the forest trail is slippery in monsoon.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Priests present dawn till dusk (per Sahasa travel account); daily devotees visit on Mondays and Sundays - not a fixed-hours site, expect daylight visiting (verify).
